newsitem.title: FRANCE: Poland officially becomes 28th OECD member.
newsitem.headline: Poland officially becomes 28th OECD member.

text.p: Poland officially became on Friday the 28th member of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development, the Paris-based club of industrialised nations announced.

"Poland officially became the 28th member company of the OECD on November 22, 1996 when it deposited its instrument of accession to the OECD Convention with the French government, depositary of the Convention," the OECD said in a statement.
Poland, which signed up for membership in July, is the third former Soviet bloc state after the Czech Republic and Hungary to join the organisation.
Poland applied on February 1, 1994 to join the group, seen as a stepping stone in its drive to be part of the European Union.
But membership was delayed by a need to pass laws meeting OECD requirements for market liberalisation.
The country hopes that the membership of the OECD will bring greater foreign investment and boost its international credit rating.
